questions.stem: A client with severe traumatic brain injury becomes progressively less responsive and develops a newly dilated unilateral pupil with worsening hypertension and bradycardia. Which nursing action has the highest priority?
questions.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Lower the head of the bed and increase stimulation to obtain another neurologic examination before notifying the trauma team of this change.","B":"Administer a high-dose corticosteroid because steroids are recommended to reduce intracranial pressure and mortality after severe traumatic brain injury.","C":"Wait for the next scheduled CT scan because neurologic deterioration is expected during the first day and does not require intervention without an ICP value.","D":"Activate urgent neurocritical evaluation for possible intracranial hypertension or herniation and prepare for time-sensitive treatment as ordered."}}
questions.rationale: Progressive neurologic deterioration and signs concerning for herniation require immediate escalation. Brain Trauma Foundation guidance supports ICP-directed management in severe TBI, recognizes the need for urgent therapy when progressive neurologic deterioration or herniation is present, and specifically states that high-dose steroids are contraindicated because they increase mortality.
questions.source_name: Brain Trauma Foundation — Guidelines for the Management of Severe TBI, 4th Edition
questions.source_detail: Current severe-TBI guidance supports ICP-directed management; progressive neurologic deterioration/herniation warrants urgent treatment, and high-dose steroids are contraindicated.

qc.qc_note: Strict Wave-5 anti-cue rule: max/min option-character ratio <=1.15; correct option is neither unique shortest nor unique longest; distractors manually reviewed for clinical plausibility and wording cues.
